## Key ideas {#ss7-key-ideas .lim-lesson .lim-key-ideas}

<div class="lim-key-row">
<h3>Terms and partial sums</h3>

$$a_n=ar^{n-1},\qquad S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}ar^{k-1}$$

</div>
<div class="lim-key-row">
<h3>Convergence condition (non-zero first term)</h3>

$$|r|<1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad-1<r<1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad r^n\longrightarrow0$$

</div>
<div class="lim-key-row">
<h3>Limiting sum</h3>

$$S_\infty=\lim_{n\to\infty}S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}ar^{k-1}=\frac{a}{1-r}\qquad(|r|<1)$$

</div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 46 · Key Ideas</p>

::: notes

Students record these mathematical statements in the booklet. Check the common multiplier and its absolute value before applying the formula. With a non-zero first term, convergence holds if and only if |r|<1. Both positive and negative ratios are allowed within this interval. Finite geometric sums have a different restriction: the quotient formula only requires r≠1, and r=1 has finite sum na. The all-zero sequence has sum 0.

:::
